questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code loads the data for each site summary? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A tenant has 250 sites with about 40 devices each. Roughly how does the number of SQL queries issued by one full iteration of `each_site_summary` scale?
choices: One query per site, about 250, because each site loads its devices
A fixed handful of queries per batch of 100 sites, independent of the number of devices
Exactly one query, because includes performs a single JOIN for everything

questions.prompt: Inside `summarize`, the code uses `site.devices.size` and `site.devices.reject(&:decommissioned_at)` rather than `site.devices.count` and `site.devices.active`. Why does that matter?
choices: `count` and `active` would run an extra SQL query for every site even though the devices are already loaded
`reject` returns an ActiveRecord relation that can still be chained lazily
`active` would exclude decommissioned devices, but `reject` includes them

questions.prompt: Why does `Reading.latest_per_device` use a separate DISTINCT ON query keyed by device ids instead of something like `has_many :readings` preloaded onto each device and then taking `device.readings.max_by(&:recorded_at)`?
choices: Preloading cannot be combined with find_in_batches
Preloading would load every reading of every device in the batch into memory just to keep one per device, which for telemetry tables is by far the largest relation
ActiveRecord does not allow a has_many association to be preloaded more than one level deep
DISTINCT ON returns the rows already sorted by recorded_at across all devices
